title: Sponsor briefing one-pager: decision cadence & QTR recap email
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, single-sheet executive sponsor briefing plus a customer-facing quarterly recap email template designed for a 20- to 30-minute sponsor touchpoint. Use for mid-cycle check-ins and as the canonical pre-read and follow-up for renewal decision-makers.

Audience:
- Executive sponsor (VP+, single point of escalation)
- Primary customer success owner (CSM)
- Solutions engineer or renewal lead (optional)

When to use:
- Quarterly business review prep when the sponsor wants a concise exec summary
- Renewal window: 90 / 60 / 30-day checkpoints mapped to decision milestones
- High-risk accounts where leadership alignment and a clear ask are needed

How to prepare (CSM checklist):
- 72 hrs before: send pre-read (one-pager) and calendar invite with 20–30 min slot
- Attach: usage trend graph, top 3 outcomes, one highlight case study (customer quote), and outstanding blockers (with owners)
- Confirm sponsor time zone and attendee list

One-pager structure (single page; can be slide 1 of QBR deck):
1) Header: Customer name | Sponsor name | CSM | Review date | Renewal window
2) Top-line impact (2–3 bullets): business outcome statements with metrics (ARR impact / cost savings / time-to-value)
3) Platform health snapshot (3 bullets): uptime/SLOs, latency/cost deltas vs. baseline, error rate trend (last 90 days)
4) Adoption signals (bulleted): active endpoints, top-5 routes by volume, percent of requests hitting cache/batch optimizations
5) Success story (1 short vignette): quick customer quote + metric (e.g., 40% faster inferencing for search feature)
6) Open risks & blockers (3 max): short description, owner, ETA to resolve
7) Immediate asks of sponsor (clear, binary where possible): e.g., prioritize integration partner meeting, approve pilot budget, sign off on renewal discount cadence
8) Renewal decision path (timeline row): 90/60/30-day checkpoints, required decision at each point, who signs, and fallback plan
9) Next meeting & CTA: proposed follow-up and very specific sponsor action (e.g., connect with procurement by DATE)

20–30 minute sponsor agenda (suggested):
- 0:00–0:03 Quick hellos and context (CSM)
- 0:03–0:08 Top-line impact & adoption highlights (CSM)
- 0:08–0:14 Open risks and remediation plan (SE / Eng owner if needed)
- 0:14–0:20 Immediate asks and decision checklist (CSM + sponsor alignment)
- 0:20–0:25 Scheduling next steps, procurement/timeline alignment (if renewal in horizon)
- 0:25–0:30 Quick wrap and confirmation of owner actions

Decision cadence (renewal window mapping):
- D-90 (Strategy sync): Confirm renewal intent, identify negotiation owner, map exec sponsors and cross-functional blockers
- D-60 (Commercial + Legal alignment): Confirm pricing envelope, required procurement timelines, early contract draft if possible
- D-30 (Sign-off readiness): Confirm final technical sign-offs, confirm PO/contract timeline, escalate any remaining blockers to sponsor

Measures of success (what to track each QBR):
- ARR retention at next renewal
- Feature adoption rate (percent of product teams using Redwood inference routes regularly)
- Latency and cost per 1k tokens relative to baseline
- Number of incidents affecting customer SLAs in the quarter

Sponsor asks template (short, clear):
- "Can you introduce us to procurement lead by [date]?"
- "Approve a 2-week pilot for Redwood Dedicated (estimated cost $X) to validate predictable throughput"
- "Block 30 minutes with your ML platform lead so we can finalize rollout timeline"

Customer-facing quarterly recap email (subject and body templates):
Subject options (pick 1):
- "QTR Recap: [Customer] & Redwood — Key outcomes and next steps"
- "[Quarter] Review: Top wins, risks, and renewal checkpoints"

Email body (concise, for exec-sponsor + procurement cc):
Hi [Sponsor name],

Thanks for the touchpoint today — quick recap below and actions we agreed. Happy to expand on any item; otherwise we’ll follow up on the CTAs.

Top outcomes this quarter:
- Outcome 1: [metric and short explanation]
- Outcome 2: [metric and short explanation]
- Outcome 3: [metric and short explanation]

Operational snapshot:
- Uptime/SLO: [value]
- Average inference latency: [value] (vs baseline [value])
- Cost per 1k tokens: [value] (improvement/decline)

Open items & owners:
- Item A — owner — ETA
- Item B — owner — ETA

Renewal checkpoints & asks:
- D-60: [what we need from customer — e.g., pricing decision, procurement contact]
- D-30: [contract sign-off and technical closeout]

Proposed next step: schedule a 30-minute commercial handoff with [procurement/contact] in the next 2 weeks.

Best,
[CSM name]

One-paragraph executive summary (for very short emails):
In [quarter], Redwood helped [customer] reduce median inference latency by X% and increased model throughput enabling [product outcome]. We’re tracking to retain the account at ARR $Y; items to resolve before renewal are [brief list].

Attachments to include with the email:
- One-pager executive briefing (PDF/slide)
- Usage dashboard screenshot (last 90 days)
- Incident summary if there was an SLA breach (short PDF)

Examples of sponsor asks phrased for execs (use exactly):
- "Please connect us to your procurement lead by 2026-04-07 so we can finalize contract terms ahead of your D-30 checkpoint."
- "Can you authorize a technical review with your ML platform lead this month so we can scope the Dedicated capacity rollout?"

Quick renewal tracker (simple text table for the one-pager):
- D-90 | Check intent | CSM (Maya) | Status: week 1 outreach
- D-60 | Commercial agreement | Sales lead (Samir) | Status: draft pricing sent
- D-30 | Contract signoff | Sponsor (name) | Status: awaiting PO

Tips & anti-patterns (do more / stop doing):
- Do: Keep the ask single-threaded per checkpoint (one clear action per stakeholder).
- Do: Quantify impact — executives respond to dollars/time saved not feature lists.
- Stop: burying open tech issues in long appendices — call them out with owners and ETA.

Mini checklist for CSM post-meeting (to be executed within 48 hours):
- Send recap email with attachments and updated one-pager
- Update renewal tracker and tag Sales/Legal owners in ticketing system
- Schedule the next checkpoint and confirm sponsor availability

Notes & provenance:
- This doc was compiled from CS playbook templates, the standard QBR framework, and interviews with two renewal managers.
- Intended to be copy-paste friendly into Google Docs and Outreach/email sequences.
